# API pointers

The **older** way over the postMessage bridge, and the one this package
deliberately did not replace. An API pointer is a name and a version; you ask
the Valu Social application for one and then call functions on it by string:

```javascript
const usersApi = await valuApi.getApi('users');   // → api:create-pointer
const me = await usersApi.run('current');         // → api:run
```

There is **no per-function API** for any of this, here or anywhere: `run` takes
a string and an object, the application looks the string up in its own registry, and
nothing checks either side. That is the difference the service SDK makes — it
has a function per service because it *carries the implementations*, and a
pointer carries nothing but the string you passed.

What that costs, concretely:

- **No parameter validation.** A misspelled field is a successful call that
  answers nothing useful.
- **No consistent argument shape.** `APIBridge.registerFunction` refuses a
  function of more than one parameter, so every pointer function takes exactly
  one — but `users.get` takes a bare `userId` string while `users.getIcon`
  takes `{userId, size}`. There is no rule; you read the app's source.
- **No ack envelope.** A pointer call rejects with whatever the application threw.
  Declared functions all resolve `{data} | {error}`
  ([callbacks-policy.md](callbacks-policy.md)).
- **Frame only.** `api:create-pointer` is a postMessage message. A headless
  agent has no application to ask, so none of this exists outside an iframe.
- **No versioning discipline in practice.** Every function below is registered
  at version 1, and `getApi(name)` without a version binds the latest.
- **Events do not cross the bridge.** A pointer module on the application's side
  emits events (`users` emits `update-user` and
  `update-user:following-status:`), and `APIPointer` here has
  `addEventListener`. Nothing connects the two: the application sends no pointer
  events over the bridge (`api:trigger` carries `on_route` and nothing else),
  so a subscription from inside an iframe never fires. Those events are real only
  for callers inside the application itself.

## The inventory

63 functions across 11 modules, vendored in
[`scripts/apiPointers.js`](../scripts/apiPointers.js) and re-measured against a
real checkout by `npm run measure:api-pointers`, which exits non-zero the
moment the app adds, renames or drops one.

| | n |
|---|---|
| modules | 11 |
| functions | 63 |
| … a declared SDK function does the same work | 15 |
| … a declared function is close but not equivalent | 7 |
| … **no declared intent: the pointer is the only way** | 41 |

So two thirds of this surface is not reachable through the service SDK at all,
and that is the answer to "what still relies on API pointers": theming and
resize, network switching, the modal stack, logout, chat-channel resolution,
removing a connection, the encryption seed, and the dock's loading and
link-blocking overrides.

The `✅ same` rows are the ones to stop using first — a declared function
covers them, with validation, caching and one failure shape, and it works
headless as well as framed.

### app

The application dock: what is installed, what is open, and how a pane behaves.

`getApi('app')` → [`src/Stores/ApplicationCenter/ApplicationCenterStoreAPI.js`](https://github.com/Roomful/valusocial-web/blob/develop/src/Stores/ApplicationCenter/ApplicationCenterStoreAPI.js)

| `run(…)` | its one argument | what it does | declared equivalent |
|---|---|---|---|
| `open` | `applicationId` | Open an application in the dock. | ✅ same `AiGuru.open` |
| `close` | `applicationId` | Close an open application. | ✅ same `AiGuru.close` |
| `expand` | `applicationId` | Expand an application pane. | ⚠️ close `Application.expand-application` |
| `hasApplication` | `applicationId` | Whether the dock knows this application at all. | ✅ same `AiGuru.has-application` |
| `isApplicationLoaded` | `applicationId` | Whether it is loaded right now — a different question. | ✅ same `AiGuru.is-application-loaded` |
| `getApplications` | `()` | Every application the dock can open, with id, slug and icon. | ✅ same `AiGuru.get-applications` |
| `getApplicationHeader` | `applicationId` | An application's title and a glyph already drawn with the platform font, for a page on another origin that cannot draw a Font Awesome class. | — none |
| `getSetting` | `key` | Read one platform setting by key. | — none |
| `navigate` | `{path}` | Navigate the Valu Social router. | — none |
| `run` | `{applicationId, action, params}` | Run an intent against another application. | — none |
| `configure-intent` | `{...}` | Open the app's intent-configuration modal. | — none |
| `notifyApplicationStateUpdated` | `{applicationId, intent}` | Tell the dock an application's state changed, so it can re-render its entry. | — none |
| `blockExternalLinks` | `block` | Stop Valu Social opening external links from this app. | — none |
| `overriderAppLoading` | `()` | Take over the application loading indicator. | — none |
| `overriderPopupLoading` | `()` | Take over the popup loading indicator. | — none |

- `close` — The declared `Application.close-application` closes the CALLER; this closes whichever id you name.
- `expand` — The declared intent expands the caller and takes no id.
- `navigate` — `api.pushRoute(path)` / `api.replaceRoute(path)` do this over `api:run-command`, which is a bridge command rather than a declared intent.
- `run` — `api.sendIntent(intent)` is the typed form, over `api:run-intent`.

### users (also `u`)

People: identity, connections, following.

`getApi('users')` — or `getApi('u')` → [`src/Stores/Application/UsersAPI.js`](https://github.com/Roomful/valusocial-web/blob/develop/src/Stores/Application/UsersAPI.js)

| `run(…)` | its one argument | what it does | declared equivalent |
|---|---|---|---|
| `current` | `()` | The signed-in user. | ✅ same `Users.current` |
| `get` | `userId` | One user model by id. | ✅ same `Users.get` |
| `getMany` | `userIds` | Several user models in one call. | — none |
| `getIcon` | `{userId, size}` | A user's avatar URL at a size, from the app's URL cache. | — none |
| `getExtended` | `userId` | The extended profile (`social:getUserProfileInfo`). | — none |
| `getLocator` | `userId` | Where the user is — the locator record (`social:getUserLocator`). | — none |
| `requestFriendship` | `userId` | Send a connection request. | ✅ same `Users.send-connection-request` |
| `cancelFriendshipRequest` | `userId` | Withdraw one you sent. | ✅ same `Users.cancel-connection-request` |
| `acceptFriendRequest` | `userId` | Accept one you received. | ✅ same `Users.accept-connection-request` |
| `declineFriendRequest` | `userId` | Decline one you received. | ✅ same `Users.decline-connection-request` |
| `deleteFriend` | `userId` | Remove an existing connection (`social:deleteFriend`). | — none |
| `getFollowersCount` | `userId` | How many followers a user has, or null when it cannot be read. | ⚠️ close `Users.search-users` |
| `follow` | `userId` | Follow a user (`social:followUser`). | — none |
| `unfollow` | `userId` | Unfollow a user (`social:unfollowUser`). | — none |

- `current` — The pointer returns the store's `baseUser`; the SDK resolves the socket's own id through `social:getUsersSimpleInfo`, because headless there is no store.
- `get` — Same RPC (`social:getUsersSimpleInfo`). The pointer takes a bare string; the SDK takes `{userId}`.
- `getMany` — The RPC accepts a list of ids; the declared `Users.get` only asks for one. A batch read is a Phase 3 candidate.
- `deleteFriend` — The manifest declares the four request transitions and not the removal, so an agent can connect people and cannot disconnect them.
- `getFollowersCount` — Same RPC (`social:searchUserFollowers`), but the declared function answers a page of users; the count is in the response the SDK discards.

### rooms

Rooms: their model, their permissions, joining and leaving.

`getApi('rooms')` → [`src/Applications/RoomsApplication/Stores/RoomsApi.js`](https://github.com/Roomful/valusocial-web/blob/develop/src/Applications/RoomsApplication/Stores/RoomsApi.js)

| `run(…)` | its one argument | what it does | declared equivalent |
|---|---|---|---|
| `getMeta` | `{roomId, networkId?}` | The basic room model. | ✅ same `Rooms.get-room` |
| `getFullModel` | `{roomId, networkId?}` | The full room model — metadata, settings, stories. | ⚠️ close `Rooms.get-room` |
| `getPermissions` | `{roomId}` | The caller's permissions in a room. | ✅ same `Rooms.get-permissions` |
| `getRoomPermissions` | `{roomId}` | The same thing again. | ✅ same `Rooms.get-permissions` |
| `getIcon` | `{roomId, size}` | A room's icon URL at a size. | — none |
| `updateMeta` | `{roomBuilder}` | Change room metadata (`room:updateMetadata`). | — none |
| `join` | `{roomId}` | Join a room. | — none |
| `leave` | `{roomId}` | Leave a room. | — none |
| `openRoomCard` | `{e, roomId}` | Open the app's room card, anchored to a click event. | — none |

- `getMeta` — Same RPC (`room:getRoomBasicModel`).
- `getFullModel` — A different RPC (`room:getRoom`). The declared function answers the BASIC model; the full one is read inside the SDK only, by the prop-order logic.
- `getPermissions` — Same RPC (`room:permissions`).
- `getRoomPermissions` — A duplicate of `getPermissions` — both emit `room:permissions`.
- `updateMeta` — Takes a live `RoomBuilder` instance, which cannot cross the bridge as JSON — so this one is internal to the Valu Social app in practice.
- `openRoomCard` — Application UI, and it takes a DOM event — not something a socket could serve.

### resources

Resources: the record, its URLs, its thumbnails.

`getApi('resources')` → [`src/Services/Resources/ResourceService.js`](https://github.com/Roomful/valusocial-web/blob/develop/src/Services/Resources/ResourceService.js)

| `run(…)` | its one argument | what it does | declared equivalent |
|---|---|---|---|
| `getResource` | `{resourceId, forceUpdate?}` | The resource record itself, from the app's own cache or the server. | — none |
| `invalidateResource` | `resourceId` | Drop the app's cached copy. | — none |
| `getResourcePath` | `{resourceId}` | The storage path of a resource. | — none |
| `getThumbnailUrl` | `{resourceId, thumbnailSize?}` | A thumbnail URL, with the decryption metadata an encrypted resource needs. | ⚠️ close `Resources.get-thumbnail-url` |
| `getResourceUrl` | `{resourceId}` | The public URL of a resource. | ⚠️ close `Resources.generate-public-url` |
| `listBotAvatars` | `{limit?}` | The network's allowed bot avatars. | ✅ same `Resources.list-bot-avatars` |

- `getThumbnailUrl` — The declared function BUILDS the URL locally (as the server does) and therefore has no decryption metadata — a known delta, recorded in parity.md. For an encrypted resource the pointer is still the only complete answer.
- `getResourceUrl` — The declared function builds the URL from `config.webBase`; this one goes through the app's own resource service.

### network

Which network the session is in, and moving between them.

`getApi('network')` → [`src/Stores/Application/NetworksAPI.js`](https://github.com/Roomful/valusocial-web/blob/develop/src/Stores/Application/NetworksAPI.js)

| `run(…)` | its one argument | what it does | declared equivalent |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | `()` | The current network id, straight from the store. | ⚠️ close `Networks.get-current-network` |
| `get` | `networkId` | Network info for the current user (`network:getNetworkInfoForUser`). | ⚠️ close `Networks.get-current-network` |
| `switch` | `networkId` | Switch the session to another network. | — none |
| `switchForRoom` | `roomId` | Switch to whichever network a room belongs to, if it is not the current one. | — none |
| `overrideNetworkSwitch` | `()` | Take over the network-switch flow. | — none |
| `startNewNetworkSession` | `{oldNetworkId, networkId, sessionId}` | Adopt a session an external system created after switching networks. | — none |

- `id` — The declared function answers `{networkId, name}` — the id is a fact of the connection, and only the name costs an RPC.
- `get` — Same RPC, but the declared function only ever asks about the CURRENT network.
- `switch` — Changes the session every other call is scoped by. Nothing in the declared surface can do this, deliberately.

## Names that collide

`dialog` is declared **twice**: once above, and again by
[`src/Services/UnityDialog/UnityDialogApi.js`](https://github.com/Roomful/valusocial-web/blob/develop/src/Services/UnityDialog/UnityDialogApi.js) with the same 2 functions (`open`, `close`).
`APIBridge.createAPi` throws on a duplicate module name, so at most one of the
two is ever live; the tables above count the pair once. 65 registrations,
63 distinct functions.

An **alias** collides silently instead — `registerAlias` just overwrites the
entry, so the last module to register the name owns it:
`chat` is registered by both `text-chat` and `auth`.
Prefer the module's own name over an alias for exactly this reason.

## What this package does and does not do about them

- `ValuApi.getApi()` and `APIPointer` are **unchanged**. Phase 1 moved the
  transport out from under them — the wire messages are byte for byte what they
  were — and Phase 2 did not touch them.
- One behaviour did change, because it was broken: `sendIntent` never settled,
  because its `api:run-completed` reply was routed as if it belonged to an
  `APIPointer`. It resolves now.
- **Nothing in the service SDK uses a pointer.** `ServiceClient` and
  `FrameCommands` both send `api:service-intent`.
- There is no plan in Phases 1–2 to wrap them. A pointer function that deserves
  to be callable from an agent should be **declared as an intent** and
  implemented here; the 41 above are the candidate list.

"Over the bridge" in all of this means the same postMessage channel every other
doc here means — [postmessage-vs-socket.md](postmessage-vs-socket.md).
